title: Wales beat New Zealand for the first time in 73 years
summary: A 35-28 win in Cardiff ended one of rugby's longest losing runs.
body:
Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 in Cardiff on Saturday 14 November, their first win over the All Blacks since 1953.

It was only the fourth time Wales have beaten New Zealand, and their biggest winning margin against them.

The match

Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit scored tries for Wales, with Sam Costelow kicking the conversions and penalties. New Zealand replied with four tries.

The match was part of rugby's new Nations Championship. About 55,000 people were in the stadium, some 20,000 short of a sell-out.

Sources: NBC Sports, ABC News (Australia), NZ Herald.
